data.title: Three points before lunch
data.situation:
Nora cleared a space on the meeting table and asked Jo to outline the plan. The topic was the hall timetable, rather than the whole history of the building. Jo’s outline had three points: what had changed, what remained open and where readers could ask questions. Nora read it as an overview before looking at the details. The dates were essential; the colour of the notice was not. The first version was intended primarily for people who already used the hall. A later article could explain the repairs to a wider audience. They stopped adding sections when the kettle clicked off. There was enough to work with. Nora: Could you outline the changes first?
Jo: I have made a short outline.
Nora: Good. The overview should help people find the details they need.

readingBlocks.zh: 诺拉清出会议桌上的一小块地方，让乔概述计划。话题是大厅的时间表，不是整栋建筑的历史。乔的提纲有三个要点：哪些变了，哪些仍开放，以及读者可以在哪里提问。诺拉先把它当作总体介绍读了一遍，再看细节。日期必不可少，通知的颜色却没那么重要。第一版主要面向已经在使用大厅的人，以后的文章可以向更多人介绍维修。水壶烧开时，她们停止增加章节，已有内容够用了。
